title: Disruption of Chlorella vulgaris Microalga Cell Wall Protocol
author: Diogo Coelho
materials: Thermostability analysis – Incubate each enzyme of the mix in a defined final concentration at the following temperatures: 30 °C, 37 °C and 40 °C to 80 °C at 5 °C intervals for 30 minutes and perform a control (no incubation). Then, cool the incubation on ice for 10 min and centrifuged at 16,100 g for 8 min at 4 °C. Recover the supernatant and quantify the protein amount in triplicate using a NanoDrop. To validate the results, analyse the supernatants by performing 14% SDS-PAGE gels.

The analysis of the oligosaccharides profile is made using a Dionex CarboPac PA10 column and electrochemical detector (ECD), according to the manufacturer's instruction method (Thermo Scientific. Dionex CarboPac PA10 in Column Product Manual).
Lyophilize 10 mg of residues for 24 hours.
Cover with the coverslip and wait 1 minute.

steps.title: Prepare C. vulgaris suspension
steps.instruction: Prepare a 20 mg/mL C. vulgaris suspension by resuspending microalgae powder in PBS buffer and mixing with a vortex.

steps.title: Prewash C. vulgaris suspension
steps.instruction: Prewash the suspension to remove impurities.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the suspension in an orbital shaker at 37ºC and 150 rpm for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the suspension at 4000 g for 30 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in new PBS buffer (20 mg/mL) and mix with a vortex.

steps.title: Add enzymes to C. vulgaris
steps.instruction: Distribute the suspension and add enzymes or controls in a 24-well plate in triplicate.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of C. vulgaris suspension to each well.
Add the respective enzyme to each well to a final concentration of 20 µg/mL.
For control wells, add 50 µL of PBS buffer instead of the enzyme.

steps.title: Incubate enzyme reactions
steps.instruction: Seal the plate and incubate in an orbital shaker at 37ºC and 60 rpm overnight.

steps.title: Recover initial supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate at 4000 g for 15 minutes and recover the supernatant into an Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Heat-treat and clarify samples
steps.instruction: Boil the recovered samples for 5 minutes, then centrifuge at 10000 g for 5 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Recover the resulting supernatant into a new Eppendorf tube for reducing sugar analysis.

steps.title: Determine reducing sugars (DNSA method)
steps.instruction: Quantify the release of reducing sugars using the DNSA reagent.

substeps.instruction: Prepare DNSA reagent: 1% 3,5-Dinitrosalicylic acid, 0.2% phenol, and 1% sodium hydroxide. Before use, add 200 µL of sodium sulphite (5%) and 2 µL of glucose (20%) per 20 mL of reagent.
Add 600 µL of the supernatant from the previous stage to a new Eppendorf and add 600 µL of the prepared DNSA reagent.
Mix vigorously and incubate in boiling water at 100ºC for 15 minutes.
Place the Eppendorfs on ice for 5 minutes.
Measure absorbance at λ=570 nm.
Calculate reducing sugars using a calibration curve with sequential dilutions of a glucose solution (initial concentration 1 mg/mL).

steps.title: Test enzyme mix
steps.instruction: Repeat the process using an enzyme mix (exo-β-glucosaminidase, alginate lyase, peptidoglycan N-acetylmuramic acid deacetylase, and lysozyme).

substeps.instruction: Repeat steps 1 through 6.
At the addition stage, use the enzyme mix where each enzyme has a final concentration of 20 µg/mL in a 1:1:1:1 ratio.

steps.title: Assess proteolysis resistance
steps.instruction: Test the resistance of the mix enzymes to porcine pancreatin.

substeps.instruction: Place 200 µL of each enzyme in the mix (at 1 g/L) into individual Eppendorfs.
For the control, add 200 µL of PBS; for the treatment, add 200 µL of porcine pancreatin (5 g/L).
Incubate reactions at 37 °C at 15 min intervals up to 2 hours.
Analyze results using 14% SDS-PAGE gels.

steps.title: Analyze supernatant components
steps.instruction: Perform various quantitative analyses on the recovered supernatants.

substeps.instruction: Reducing sugars: Repeat the DNSA method steps.

Fatty acids: Lyophilize 1 mL of supernatant for 24 hours. Extract lipids using dichloromethane:methanol (2:1, v/v) per Folch et al. (1957) and Carlson (1985). Esterify fatty acids to FAME using acetylchloride-methanol solution at 80 °C for 60 min. Analyze FAME per Coelho et al. (2019).
Oligosaccharides: Inject 10 µL of supernatant directly into HPLC. Quantify using a glucose standard curve (0.025 mM to 0.2 mM).
Protein: Determine content using the classic Kjeldahl method (AOAC, 2000).
Pigments: Determine antioxidant pigments (chlorophylls a, b, and carotenoids) following Hynstova et al. (2018).

steps.title: Analyze microalgae residue
steps.instruction: Recover the residue after the first centrifugation (step 5) and perform analysis.

substeps.instruction: Fatty acids: Repeat the lyophilization, extraction, and esterification steps used for the supernatant.

Cell counting: Resuspend 10 mg of residue in 500 µL PBS buffer. Add 2 mL PBS and homogenize with 'up and down' micropipette movements. Add 20 µL of homogenate to a Neubauer chamber and count cells via optical microscope.

Fluorescence intensity: Add 10 µL of the homogenate to a slide. Add 2 µL Calcofluor White stain and 2 µL potassium hydroxide (10%). Observe under fluorescence microscope (400×, DAPI filter) and quantify intensity using Image J software.
